deviations: The packet prescribes face A = `Cone` mirror and face B = `Plane` mirror in one two-face shell, but `Shell<P, C, S>` stores `Vec<Face<P, C, S>>` and `wedge::check` is generic over a single surface type `S` (wedge.rs `check` signature); a cone face and a plane face cannot share one shell. Realized the packet's geometry with a test-only delegating enum `Surface { Plane(Plane), Cone(Cone) }` in the `mod tests` block that forwards `ParametricSurface`, `ParametricSurface3D` and `SearchParameter<D2>` to the two witnesses; face A carries `Surface::Cone(...)`, face B carries `Surface::Plane(...)`. The underlying surfaces are exactly the packet's `Cone` and `Plane` mirrors.

Test 1's plane: the packet suggests the plane through (1,0,1), (-1,0,-1), (0,1,0) (marked 'e.g.'). That plane's normal is (1,0,-1)/sqrt(2), which equals the cone's normal along the generator, so the two surfaces are tangent (folded wedge, sin = 0) and the sample at t0=(1,0,1) refuses as `Contradictory` before the apex midpoint is ever sampled. Used the plane through (1,0,1), (-1,0,-1), (0,1,1) instead: it contains the whole shared edge, is not tangent (wedge sine 0.577 at the endpoints, clearing the 0.5 margin), and still reaches the apex at the midpoint so the singular normal refuses with `NumericallyUnresolved`.
disagreements: The packet names the target file and module `wedge.rs` / `wedge::check` throughout (write_allow, prose, and anchors A3-A5's `grep -c ... vendor/truck/truck-topology/src/invariants/wedge.rs`). The tree's file and module are `wedge.rs` / `wedge::check`; no `wedge.rs` exists. The anchor patterns all match the real `wedge.rs` with the expected counts (A1=1, A2=1, A3=1, A4=1, A5=1).

The packet's 'face A = `Cone` mirror, face B = `Plane` mirror' in a single two-face shell contradicts the code: `Shell<P, C, S>` and `check<P, C, S>` require one surface type for the whole shell, so the two distinct witnesses cannot be faces of one shell without a common carrier (see the first deviation for the delegating wrapper used).
notes: Pre-fix failing observation (recorded on the buggy code, tests added before the repair): `wedge_singular_midpoint_normal_refuses` FAILED returning Ok(Certified { props: [(WedgeNonDegeneracy, True)], method: Float, ... }) -- the cone-apex midpoint normal normalizes to NaN and `NaN < sin_margin` is false in IEEE, so the refusal arm never fired and the knife edge at the singular point was silently certified; `wedge_singular_endpoint_with_finite_midpoint_refuses` FAILED returning the same Ok certificate -- midpoint-only sampling found a finite midpoint normal with a well-defined wedge (sine 0.577) against the plane and certified a hold even though the t=0 endpoint is the apex. Both regressions now PASS after the repair. Repair: `surface_normal` computes the normal's magnitude by hand and returns `Refusal::NumericallyUnresolved` when it is not finite or is zero (no reliance on `normalize()`); `test_edge` samples the parameter-range endpoints `t0`, `t1` and the midpoint `t_mid`, requiring every sample to project onto both faces, clear the margin with finite normals, and refusing `NumericallyUnresolved` when the cross-product magnitude (sin_angle) is not finite (Contradictory when it is finite and below the margin). Refusal shape unchanged (existing `unresolved()` helper, `UncertifiedContainment`), certificate still `Method::Float`. API-bound limitation (owner-approved scope amendment): the certificate's claim is the wedge condition at the SAMPLED parameters, not the whole edge; a whole-edge interval certificate is not expressible through this checker's generic `S` bounds (ParametricSurface + ParametricSurface3D + SearchParameter, which have no interval-normal capability) and additionally needs the edge's parameter image on each face (the pcurve, BG-CE-001's unwired payload) -- the module doc now states the three-sample scope and the not-a-whole-edge caveat. Pre-existing tests (tent holds, coplanar violate, doubled-back violate, boundary skipped, projection unresolved) all remain green: the tent clears the 0.5 margin at all three samples, and the fold/crack witnesses fold at every point of the shared edge so all samples refuse.
